title: Saag Aloo
subtitle: Indian spiced spinach and potato
excerpt: The North Indian spinach and potato dry curry: potatoes fried until golden in spiced oil, then folded with wilted spinach and a little ginger and garlic until everything is combined in a rich, well-seasoned dry side dish.

recipe.sourceNotes: Saag aloo (saag means leafy greens, aloo means potato) is a staple of North Indian and Punjabi cooking, widely made at home and in restaurants throughout the subcontinent and the diaspora. The saag can be spinach (palak), mustard greens (sarson), or a mixture of greens; spinach is the most common variety internationally. The distinction between palak aloo and saag aloo is sometimes made in Indian cooking: palak aloo uses pure spinach, often blended; saag aloo uses whole or roughly chopped mixed greens. The version here uses whole spinach leaves rather than a purée for a more rustic texture. The potatoes are typically fried before the greens are added to develop their exterior before the steam from the spinach cooks them through.

recipeTools.notes: A wide, heavy frying pan or casserole.

content.text: Par-boil the potatoes until just tender before frying; this ensures they are cooked through without burning on the outside during the frying stage. Fresh spinach reduces to about a quarter of its raw volume: use more than you think you need. The dish should be relatively dry; if there is too much liquid from the spinach, cook uncovered on high heat to evaporate it.

items.preparation: peeled and cut into 3 cm cubes; par-boiled for 8 minutes and drained
fresh, washed; or frozen, thawed and squeezed dry

content.text: Heat the oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the cumin seeds and mustard seeds and fry for 30 seconds until they pop. Add the onion and cook for 10 minutes until golden. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute. Add the turmeric, coriander, and chilli powder and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the potato pieces and fry over medium-high heat for 8 to 10 minutes. Turn them every few minutes. They should be golden and slightly crisp on the outside when done.

Add the fresh spinach in large handfuls, stirring to wilt each batch. Once all the spinach has wilted, cook for 3 to 4 minutes until any excess liquid has evaporated. Add the garam masala and lemon juice. Taste and adjust the salt. Serve as a side dish with dal and rice or roti.
